capture.instance: A scratch home, never the install's own: seed core's demo home into it and run a gateway on a free loopback port (PERSONALCLAW_HOME=/tmp/pc-showcase personalclaw gateway --seed demo-home --seed-replace --port 10021 --no-open --json-ready), as core's docs/screenshots/CAPTURE.md describes. The seed carries projects, tasks, knowledge documents and markdown memory, and binds no model, so install a model app and bind chat (and embedding and speech-to-text, so no surface waits on a model) before any turn. Chat, the approval, the loop, the skill proposal, the artifacts and the memory records are the product of real turns on that model, a few short ones; nothing is staged. Then photograph each appView with scripts/capture-app-shots.mjs, which signs its browser in with the gateway's token.
capture.notes: All shots come from the one home, so they read as one workspace. Capture against a RELEASED tag build, never an unmerged branch, and review every PNG in marketing/.captures/ before promoting it into src/assets/.

shots.appView: Inbox (the unified attention surface, with kind filter chips)
shots.scenario: A real queue of what waits on you, with three kinds of item, because the point is that these used to live in different places: a goal loop asking which of two fixes to apply, a tool approval the agent is waiting on, and a proposed skill awaiting approval, each with its deep link to where it came from, and the filter chips along the top showing the kinds present. NOT an empty or single-kind inbox — a one-kind inbox looks like the old notification list and tells the reader nothing.
shots.value: Everything waiting on you — loop decisions, proposals, approvals, alerts — in one place you can answer in, instead of a toast that scrolls past while the work stays stalled.

shots.scenario: The rules matrix with a REALISTIC spread of choices rather than all-defaults, so the four modes are legible: something noisy set to digest (heartbeats), something important on notify (loop needs input), something on badge, and one set to never. If a keyword/name-mention condition is configured, show it — that is the part that now works for loop requests and proposals, not just channel messages. Since 0.2.3 only approvals, questions and errors notify by default and everything else is a badge, so the reset marks sit on the rows set away from that.
shots.value: A row per kind of notification with four choices — notify, badge, digest, never — so quietening one noisy kind no longer means raising the bar for everything.

shots.scenario: A populated library showing a MIX of artifact types the agent produced — a document, a spreadsheet, a chart and a markdown deliverable — with live previews where the kind has one, plus a collection grouping some of them. The variety is the point: it should be obvious these are real outputs the agent produced, not stock thumbnails.
shots.value: Everything the agent produced, previewable and searchable, grouped into collections — instead of files scattered through a chat log.

clips.scenario: Home showing what needs you, with at least one approval and one question waiting; held still about 4 s.

One chat turn from the prompt sent to the reply finished: the turn's status row above the composer, its orb and its turning word while the agent thinks and reads a file, then the reply and its done mark; about 45 s on a local model.
A goal loop's cockpit while it plans ("Planning") and then runs a cycle; about 8 s.
A pending approval card, and the turn's status row with its "!" badge and "Needs your OK", held still; about 4 s.
Tab to the pending approval card, press Cmd Enter, and it resolves; about 6 s.
In a running loop's cockpit, press Pause, it settles paused, then Resume; about 6 s.
In Apps, open one app that needs no key, read its consent dialog, install, and it shows installed; about 6 s.

Core's demo click-path at the release (docs/demo/CLICKPATH.md, docs/demo/capture_demo.mjs), end to end: Home, Chat, Approval, Loops, Knowledge, Artifacts and back to Home, about 85 s, with each beat's start time recorded for the composition's data-media-start.
